purpose: Evaluate whether monocular geometry predictions can provide a stable AI-origin signal. This audit does not evaluate P0 line-family visualisation.

runtime_protocol.isolation: Each 12-image shard loads the model once in a foreground Python process and then exits.
runtime_protocol.feature_constraint: Only line geometry sampled from the predicted normal field; no RGB pixels, metadata, P3 score, or provenance signal.

fixed_diagnostic_protocol.orientation_source: DeepFloyd indoor train, six real and six generated images
untouched_tests: SDXL indoor test, six real and six generated images
SDXL outdoor test, six real and six generated images
fixed_diagnostic_protocol.method: For each of eleven predeclared geometry features, select only its score direction on DeepFloyd, then report rank AUC unchanged on each SDXL scene.
fixed_diagnostic_protocol.limitations: Six images per class per set is deliberately a low-cost rejection screen, not an accuracy estimate or an integration acceptance test.

decision.reason: The strongest features on the independent DeepFloyd direction-selection set collapse or reverse on isolated SDXL indoor and outdoor scenes. This is incompatible with a stable source signal and is far below the 0.80 validation target.
decision.retained_use: The bounded MoGe probe may remain a future explanatory geometry research tool, but it must not contribute to the product's AI-likelihood conclusion.
decision.next_action: Do not run a full multi-hour feature extraction unless a new, preregistered source-classification hypothesis has a separate validation protocol.
